hypothesis: Rust supervisor-config pre-bind write performs a temp-file fsync that TS does not request; on the measured VM, sync_all accounts for 30.9–103.6ms of a 31–104ms Supervisor::new under slow-flush disk conditions. Remove only that extra sync while keeping atomicity, permissions, pre-bind failure behavior, wire/session semantics.
approach: In crates/pa-daemon/src/descriptor.rs, persist_supervisor_config exclusively calls write_file_atomic_unsynced: create temporary file, buffered write+flush, restrict to 0600, atomic rename, and clean temp on failure. All worker descriptor and update-prepare durable writes retain write_file_atomic with sync_all. Supervisor::new still persists before socket bind; no startup work was moved. Unit tests pin replace/0600/temp-cleanup and e2e tests pin persisted contents and fail-before-bind on injected rename error. Post-bind predecessor attempt is REVERTED; see 20260926-005642-daemon-boot-config-persist-off-accept-path.json.
parity_notes: TS packages/coding-agent/src/utils/atomic-file.ts:65 fsyncs only if options.fsync is requested, closes descriptor before rename (:66–72); TS daemon-supervisor.ts:1739 persists supervisor config without fsync option, :869 invokes it before listen. TS :839/:1712–30 DOES read persisted defaultSessionConfig upon construction/restart, while Rust descriptor::load_supervisor_config currently has no callers and Rust payload is defaultSessionDir rather than TS defaultSessionConfig: this pre-existing port gap is NOT a cross-product no-reader claim. Rust Supervisor::new persists before socket bind; failure-before-bind unchanged. Atomic replace, permissions, persisted payload and no-temp postcondition tested. Removing sync_all weakens Rust crash durability (power-loss may lose newest config despite atomic rename); TS has the same no-fsync setting but this is still a deliberate downgrade from previous Rust behavior. Rust currently re-derives session dir rather than recovering it from config; worker descriptor and update-prepare writes retain sync. RLM API/wire/session replay unchanged by this patch. Tested on Linux VM; macOS arm64 behavior not measured here. Windows not shipped in frozen hillclimb.
